source_text: «Τότε προσηνέχθησαν αὐτῷ παιδία» ἕως τοῦ ἐπιθεῖναι τὰς χεῖρας. Οἱ ἐν Χριστῷ νήπιοι καὶ θηλάζοντες ἀεὶ προσφέρονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ· «Γάλα ὑμᾶς ἐπότισα, οὐ βρῶμα.» Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα ὁ πλούσιος νεανίσκος ἐρωτᾷ περὶ ζωῆς αἰωνίου· «Εἰ θέλεις τέλειος εἶναι, ὕπαγε πώλησον…» λυπούμενος δὲ ἀπῆλθε διὰ τὰ χρήματα. «Δυσκόλως πλούσιος εἰσελεύσεται εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν»· οὐκ εἶπεν ἀδύνατον, ἀλλὰ δύσκολον· «Εὐκοπώτερον κάμηλον διὰ τρυπήματος ῥαφίδος.» Πολλοὶ δὲ ἔσονται πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι καὶ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι· ἡ παραβολὴ τῶν ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι ἐργατῶν δηλοῖ τοὺς καθ’ ὥραν κληθέντας ἴσον τὸν μισθὸν λαμβάνοντας. Δόξα Χριστῷ. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: Infants, the rich young man, and the workers' equal wage
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew 19:13-30, moving from the blessing of the children to the rich young man's question and the parable of the workers in the vineyard.
pass_a_gloss: "Then children were brought to him" up to the laying on of hands. The infants in Christ and those nursing are always brought to Jesus: "I gave you milk to drink, not solid food." After these things the rich young man asks about eternal life: "If you wish to be perfect, go, sell..." but grieving he went away because of the possessions. "With difficulty a rich man will enter into the kingdom of heaven"; he did not say impossible, but difficult: "Easier for a camel through the eye of a needle." But many first will be last and last first: the parable of the workers in the vineyard shows those called at each hour receiving equal pay. Glory to Christ. Amen.

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for regnum caelorum; the Greek here is the Matthean phrase.
Distinguishes νήπιοι from παιδία (children); Origen uses the Pauline milk metaphor for spiritual immaturity.
Keeps the participle's force as the reason he went away; not merely 'sad' but actively sorrowing.
Origen's point is the contrast with 'impossible'; 'difficult' preserves the exact negation he emphasizes.
Standard rendering for the parable's laborers; keeps the economic sense of hired hands.

pass_b_english: "Then children were brought to him" up to the laying on of hands. Those who are infants in Christ and still nursing are always brought to Jesus: "I gave you milk to drink, not solid food" (1 Corinthians 3:2). After this the rich young man asks about eternal life: "If you want to be perfect, go, sell..." (Matthew 19:21). But he went away grieving because of his possessions. "A rich person will enter the kingdom of heaven with difficulty" (Matthew 19:23). He did not say it was impossible, but difficult: "It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle" (Matthew 19:24). And many who are first will be last, and the last first (Matthew 19:30). The parable of the workers in the vineyard shows those called at each hour receiving equal pay. Glory to Christ. Amen.
